source: **real** Grok Build 1.0.13 (5e9a58528b76, stable) tool-permission prompt,
        2026-09-01, isolated tmux server (`tmux -L gc1` with a private
        TMUX_TMPDIR, 120x40), `grok --permission-mode default` in a scratch
        directory. The account's Grok Build inference balance was exhausted
        (HTTP 402 on every model), so the tool call that raises the prompt came
        from a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint declared as a `[model.*]` entry;
        everything below is drawn by Grok's own permission UI from a
        `run_terminal_command` call for `echo hello`, held open by an
        `ask = ["Bash(echo *)"]` rule. Nothing was approved.
why: this file replaces a synthetic fixture that guessed the prompt's shape from
     the deleted pre-manifest rule `grok.screen.blocked`, whose alternation held
     `Allow .*\?` and `Enter to confirm`. Grok 1.0.13 renders no screen of that
     shape: its permission prompt is the ┃-guttered option dialog upstream
     already describes, and three upstream blockers reach it —
     `osc_title_blocked` (1300) on the "⚠ Action Required" title,
     `option_dialog_blocked` (1200) on the numbered ┃ rows, and
     `permission_scope_selector` (1180) on "Yes, proceed" / "No, reject" over the
     "←/→:scope" footer. `sidecar.allow_prompt_blocked` (1130) neither fires nor
     is needed here. See manifests/sidecar/grok.toml and
     docs/reference/herdr-detection-parity.md.
shape: reduced from the 40-row capture to its evidence rows — the context/path
       header, the clock, the user's own prompt row and the empty scrollbar rows
       are dropped and trailing whitespace is stripped; every retained row is
       verbatim, including the footer, which the 120-column pane truncates at
       "Esc:".

pane_height: 40
state: blocked
